# Explicit endomorphism project study

One unchanged complete first source records ordinary-project refusal of
`Op<Bit -> Bit>` before the adapter repair. The existing common judgment already
normalizes equal ports; the finite profile ignored that result and rejected
every explicit codomain. The later check and run use the same source and return
classical one through fresh native acceptance.

Independent regressions compare abbreviation and explicit spelling for Bit,
Unit scalar phase kickback, ordered product action and adjoint cancellation.
False Meaning and same-width different-tree ports still reject; unused general
arrows retain their profile refusal. No new syntax or acceptance rule is added.

The first Rust test used packed `controlled(U)(q)`, exposing a separate existing
finite-adapter arity refusal even with the abbreviated kind. That failed log is
retained outside fixtures. Its scalar test now uses the existing two-argument
control application to isolate spelling equivalence; packed-control integration
is not claimed complete. This is informed work, not a blind model benchmark.
General-arrow finite lowering, rectangular Meaning, #83/#46 and broader proof
obligations remain open.
